findings.title_text: Possible s.201(1A) interest on a 194H shortfall for one payee -- 1 tranche -- range pending deposit evidence
limits_text: Books/documents alone cannot establish the actual deduction/collection and deposit dates; challans, the TAN and (for the pre-deduction leg) Form 26A are needed before any single interest amount can be confirmed -- this is a range, not a computed liability.

Tie this range to the quarterly TDS statement (Form 26Q) filed for each credit: TRACES computes s.201(1A) interest from the dates of credit or payment and of deduction reported there. Where the statement reports other dates, or omits a credit, the route is a correction statement filed through TRACES; the interest then follows the dates as corrected.

Where the date of deduction is not known, the interest is computed two ways as at 2026-09-30. If the tax is still not deducted: at the pre-deduction rate to 2026-09-30. If it was deducted and not deposited: the largest amount over every possible date of deduction up to 2026-09-30, at the pre-deduction rate to that date and the post-deduction rate from it; a month that both periods touch is counted at both rates. Both count calendar months or part of one, and no month after 2026-09-30; a count by periods of thirty days is not computed and may give a higher figure.
No payee return-filing date was supplied, so the Form 26A (first proviso to s.201(1)) relief scenario could not be computed for this row.

Taken on the credits that attract TDS under s.194H (as read here, pending the CA's confirmation of that reading): once the payee's aggregate in the financial year exceeds the limit, every credit, the earlier ones from the date the aggregate is crossed. The aggregate is gross and a crossing is never undone: a reversal lowers nothing. One the client's list classifies as reversing a particular bill, or as an error, is named on the payee's finding but not applied, pending bill-wise detail from the books.

Whether this payee's credits were foreseeable is not classified in the client's list of payees, so the maximum runs each credit's tax from its own date. If the work was genuinely one-off, the CA may instead run the earlier credits from the day the year's total crossed the limit: classify the payee to show that range.

Whether this assessee is a deductor at all for the year is itself unresolved (previous-year turnover unconfirmed -- see tds_payees' own deductor_status finding); this interest range is conditional on deductor status being confirmed, not a standalone conclusion.
ask_client_text: Provide TDS/TCS challans and the TAN to confirm actual deduction/collection and deposit dates for this payee.
If not deducted/collected, confirm whether Form 26A (or the equivalent TCS relief) is available, and the payee's own return-filing date.
